name: Name familiar shapes
description: Student can name familiar shapes: circle, square, triangle and rectangle.
exampleOfSuccess: Shown shape cards, the student names the circle, square, triangle and rectangle.
commonError: Student calls any round shape a circle or any four-sided shape a square.
checkpointTask: Show familiar shape cards. Ask the student to name each.

name: Find shapes in everyday objects
description: Student can recognise and name familiar shapes within objects in the environment.
exampleOfSuccess: The student points out the circle on a clock and the rectangle of a door.
commonError: Student only recognises shapes on cards, not in real objects.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to find and name familiar shapes in objects around the room.

name: Sort shapes into groups and say why
description: Student can sort a collection of shapes into groups by a feature and give a reason.
exampleOfSuccess: The student sorts shapes into 'round' and 'has corners' and explains the rule.
commonError: Student sorts by colour or size, or cannot say the rule they used.
checkpointTask: Give a mixed set of shapes. Ask the student to sort them and say why they grouped them that way.

name: Make a picture using shapes
description: Student can create a picture using a variety of shapes.
exampleOfSuccess: The student makes a house from a square and a triangle, and a sun from a circle.
commonError: Student uses only one shape, or cannot name the shapes they used.
checkpointTask: Give the student a set of shapes. Ask them to make a picture and name the shapes they used.

name: Describe a familiar shape
description: Student can describe a familiar shape, such as whether it is round or has corners and sides.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says a triangle has three corners and three straight sides.
commonError: Student describes a shape only by what it looks like ('like a hat') rather than its features.
checkpointTask: Show a shape. Ask the student to describe it, such as its corners and sides.

name: Use position words
description: Student can use position words such as inside, underneath, on top of, next to and behind.
exampleOfSuccess: Asked where the cat is, the student says it is underneath the table.
commonError: Student uses vague words like 'there' instead of position words.
checkpointTask: Place an object in different positions. Ask the student to use a position word to say where it is.

name: Describe where an object is
description: Student can describe the position of an object in relation to another object.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says the ball is next to the box and behind the chair.
commonError: Student names the objects but not how they are positioned relative to each other.
checkpointTask: Set up objects around the room. Ask the student to describe where each one is.

name: Describe their own position
description: Student can describe where they are in relation to objects or people around them.
exampleOfSuccess: Standing in the room, the student says 'I am in front of the door and next to Sam'.
commonError: Student describes the room generally rather than their own position in it.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to describe where they are standing in relation to things around them.

name: Describe how they moved
description: Student can describe where they have moved themselves or an object within a space.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says 'I moved the chair from next to the desk to behind the door'.
commonError: Student says they moved without describing the start and end positions.
checkpointTask: After the student moves themselves or an object, ask them to describe where it started and ended.
